name: g2-fpm-realapps-8510-php
status: RCE confirmed on the private realapps 8.5.10 target (php session serializer, zif_system); ASLR off; one-shot worker crash; clean zif_passthru real-target run pending

type_word_after_write.meaning: zval IS_LONG type word written by php_var_unserialize; php_session_normalize_vars later zeroes it. The value word at 0x22c54c8 keeps 0xa3c061 (the decode pointer).

zif_route.symbol_verification: nm -an and readelf -sW on the installed realapps binary: zif_system 0xa3c061, zif_passthru 0xa3c074, php_exec_ex 0xa3bdfd, php_exec 0xa3bbd7, php_session_decode 0x9e68b5, ps_srlzr_decode_php 0x9e6fae, ps_serializers 0x22c54a0, ps_globals 0x22d0dc0. A file-offset dump at 0x1cc54a0 confirms the three ps_serializers entries.

zif_system.behavior: one-shot: the command executes through php_exec_ex -> php_exec -> popen, then php_exec writes the return zval through return_value=ZSTR_LEN(data); SIGSEGV at php_exec+466

zif_passthru.behavior: symbol verified; expected clean because type 3 never writes return_value. The realapps clean run is pending and is not claimed here.
zif_passthru.delta_from_zif_system: +0x13 on this build, not the +0x10 seen on the four lab profiles

fake_execute_data.s_0x18: F; set as specified, not dereferenced on the direct decode path
fake_execute_data.f_0xc8: not set and not used; the measured zend_internal_function.handler is at +0x58 on this binary, but the direct decode callback never dispatches through execute_data->func or a handler slot
fake_execute_data.parse_requirement: num_args==1, arg1 type IS_STRING (6), F readable, F+0x10 == strlen(F+0x18), length non-zero, no embedded NUL

record.shape: 18 filler strings k0..k17, one forged-name variable with a 768-byte name and a 1.9 MB value, then z
record.offsets_relative_to: S = ZSTR_VAL(data) of the second decode buffer
record.note: The 768-byte forged name is the fake execute_data at S=ZSTR_VAL(data); F is name+0x200. The 1.9 MB value of that variable is copied to vo=chunk+0x1018 and covers P=chunk+0x18c000 and B0f=chunk+0x2018. The receipt's scripts/mkrec.py builds this record; the generic --step g2 builder emits the php_binary G6 shape and rejects this profile.

producer.result: HTTP 200, 276 B; OOM at 1073741824 bytes (tried to allocate 5242880) in EntityContentDataCodec.php:210
producer.stale_state: BG(unserialize).level=1, data=P=0x7ffff218c000, B0=0x7ffff219e000, used_slots=1; the consumer must be the next request on the same worker

crash.fault_address_meaning: 1,901,104 = ZSTR_LEN(data); the address is inside the binary r--p mapping 0x01000000-0x01eac000
crash.cause: the decode ABI passes rsi=ZSTR_LEN(data) but zif_system treats rsi as zval *return_value; php_exec unconditionally stores the empty-string return zval there after popen

respawn.http: nginx returned 502 (157 B); a later GET /index.php?title=Main_Page returned 200
respawn.pool: the pool survived; only the worker that ran the exploit died

zif_route.clean_run: pending; zif_passthru is symbol verified at 0xa3c074 but no realapps clean run is claimed

md5_lock: select this profile only when the target binary md5 matches; a mismatch invalidates every offset

ps_serializers.note: the active handler is php (ps_serializers[1]). F12b writes zif_system into its decode field. The php decode slot is 8 mod 16, but the fake var_dtor_entries base B0f is also 8 mod 16, so the negative-K slot is exact. The generic G2/G6 php_binary builder assumes a 16 byte aligned target; this profile is descriptive for F12b and is rejected by --step g2.

ps_serializer_slot.note: PS(serializer) points at the active ps_serializer entry (0x22c54b8). F12b writes the static ps_serializers[1].decode field instead: a 16-byte typed write at 0x22d0f20 would place its type word at 0x22d0f28, overwriting http_session_vars.value.

decode_call.note: ps_globals+0x160 holds 0x22c54b8; the call reads decode at +0x10 = 0x22c54c8. The decode ABI passes rsi=len; zif_system treats it as zval *return_value, so php_exec writes the return zval to the length address.

write.bound: only used_slots + num > 255 rejects; negative used_slots pass
write.second_slot: target + 16 = 0x22c54d8 (php_binary.encode; not written by the single z target)

adjacent_slots.target + 16: php_binary.encode (0x22c54d8); not written by the single z target
adjacent_slots.target + 24: php_binary.decode (0x22c54e0); not touched by this record

write.value_form: i:<n>; parses an IS_LONG zval, so the written pointer is an arbitrary 64 bit value; F12b writes 10731617 = 0xa3c061
write.alignment: target 0x22c54c8 is 8 mod 16 and B0f 0x7ffff2002018 is 8 mod 16, so target - (B0f + 0x10) is divisible by 16. The generic G2/G6 builder assumes a 16 byte aligned target because it places fake B0 at the 16 byte aligned stale B0.

record.command_rule: the 64-byte command is NUL-free; F+0x10 is its strlen; there is no php_binary 32-byte padding and no trailing #
record.payload_placement: the 1.9 MB value of the forged-name variable is copied to vo=chunk+0x1018 and covers both P=chunk+0x18c000 and B0f=chunk+0x2018

lab_geometry.note: the first decode buffer X is not recorded in the receipt; X2/S are the second, re-encoded buffer

heap_leak.measured_relation: no ASLR capable heap leak; the F12b producer geometry is ASLR off and fixed

staticleak.verdict: save path control and static serving proven; M11 encode overread failed; no heap pointer or B0 recovered

heap_leak.note: the F12b proof needs operator supplied X2, P, B0f and the exact record length; it does not demonstrate ASLR-on or internet exploitation

prerequisites: md5 locked: the installed binary must match 4ee099823b75e16ea36f93c71d57bfd8
non PIE target (ET_EXEC) so ps_serializers is at a fixed address
setarch x86_64 -R (ASLR off) and the measured chunk/P/B0 geometry

producer: anonymous POST /api.php with contentmodel=wikibase-item and contentformat=application/vnd.php.serialized plus the 500 KB probe; OOM at the 1024 MiB limit leaves BG(unserialize).level=1 and the stale P/B0
the consumer must be the immediately following request on the same worker; any intervening request resets BG(unserialize) at RINIT
session.serialize_handler=php; session.upload_progress.enabled=1 with the forced END update in the same request
record: 18 filler strings, one 768-byte forged-name variable with a 1.9 MB value, then z|i:10731617; exact total length 36101091
single shot per plant: the static decode pointer stays poisoned; the worker must be restarted
zif_system is one-shot; a clean zif_passthru real-target run is pending
no ASLR capable heap leak is demonstrated; a real internet target still needs the leak
caveats: private lab only: ASLR off via setarch x86_64 -R; no ASLR-on and no internet exploitation is claimed
zif_system is one-shot: the command runs, then php_exec writes the return zval through return_value=ZSTR_LEN(data); the worker SIGSEGVs at php_exec+466 and the FPM master respawns it
the decode ABI (char *buf, size_t len) does not match zif_system(execute_data, return_value): rsi=len becomes return_value. No fake execute_data field can fix this for type=1
a writable len (>= about 0x2200000) conflicts with the 2 MiB cached-chunk overlap that carries the fake P/B0/B0f; no survival variant was found or attempted
the static decode pointer remains poisoned in the worker after the request; the next session decode would re-enter zif_system with a different length. Worker restart is required
a direct PS(serializer) overwrite at 0x22d0f20 would put the zval type word at 0x22d0f28 (http_session_vars.value); F12b targets the static ps_serializers[1].decode field instead
F+0xc8 is not used on this path; the measured zend_internal_function.handler is at +0x58, but the decode callback is invoked directly and never dereferences execute_data->func
the realapps clean zif_passthru run is pending; only the symbol at 0xa3c074 is verified. Do not claim a surviving realapps worker until that run is recorded
the generic --step g2 builder emits the php_binary G6 record and rejects this profile (record_builder=php_session_zif); the F12b record comes from the receipt's scripts/mkrec.py
no claim is made for other session savers, opcache, ZTS or shared pools
